source.title: The First Token Is a Clue: Verbalizing Multi-Token Concepts from the J-lens

page_placements.theme: Latent multi-hop and intermediate computation within one forward pass

record.tranche_reason: Extends investigation of latent intermediate concepts to synthetic multi-hop cloze tasks and tests their causal effect on answers; it does not use the rhyme-planning method.
record.gate_note: The paper measures readout of annotated intermediate concepts and tests concept-swap interventions on answers. These results bear on V5's multi-step-task setting, but do not test rhyming, future-token prediction from one state, pre-caching, or planning in chess or Sokoban.
record.test_reason: This is a readout-method paper (Concept Lens). Its results measure how well its own pipeline retrieves annotated bridge concepts in multi-hop clozes, and whether its derived directions can swap answers. The bridge concept is computed for the current answer, not a planned future output, so no result bears on look-ahead or planning. Future Lens, one of the original sources, is cited only as motivation in Appendix G.6. The reader's T3/V5 link is not supported: latent multi-hop recall of an intermediate entity is a related but different construct from internal look-ahead, and Rank@10 is bounded by the method's own proposal coverage (oracle-candidate Rank@10 is 80.2–98.8%), not by the model's behaviour.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors present Concept Lens as a lightweight multi-token readout method. It retrieves annotated intermediate concepts across five models, and concept swaps shift answers in predicted directions. They add that candidate coverage is the main bottleneck, and that the annotated concepts are not guaranteed to be represented in the model's computation. They make no claim about planning or look-ahead.
record.recipe_differences: Uses lens-guided candidate generation, carrier-derived concept representations, source-state scoring, and concept-swap interventions on paired multi-hop clozes; unlike the original rhyme-planning claim, it does not study verse or candidate future rhyme words.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and by J-lens versus R-lens. The paper also reports that prompt form affects readout rates in its answer-cued diagnostic.

fits_no_version.finding: On 2,400 multi-hop clozes across five instruction-tuned models (8B–70B), annotated unnamed intermediate concepts are retrievable from mid-layer states. Oracle-candidate Rank@10 is 80.2–98.8% with J-lens; end-to-end is 23.1–61.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Latent multi-hop reasoning: models internally represent unstated bridge concepts before producing the answer.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing the source bridge-concept direction with the partner's moves the answer to the partner answer in 15.7–59.4% of trials (CS@10), versus 0.8–1.6% for random directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intermediate bridge-concept representations causally mediate multi-hop answers.

record.problems: The benchmark is synthetic and uses annotated intermediate concepts; the authors note ground truth concepts are not guaranteed to be represented in the model's computation. Causal interventions are deliberately applied, so they establish effects of edited concept directions rather than spontaneous planning frequency. Rank@10 and clean-swap success are incomplete and no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Table 3 S@10 values, add-only and delete-only CS@10 values, and the Template Lens and random-direction P@10 values; Table 2 Coverage and oracle-candidate results; and additional appendix diagnostics and prompt-form results. The retained rows prioritize end-to-end concept readout, full-replacement partner promotion and clean swaps, and operation-control partner promotion.

untested.parts: No verse, rhyme, or frontier-model planning test.
No prediction of tokens several positions ahead from one hidden state. Future Lens is only cited.
No test of features computed for later positions versus next-token side effects.
No rhyme-planning test in open models.
No look-ahead measure. Multi-hop clozes read a bridge concept used for the immediate answer, not a plan for future tokens. No chess, Sokoban, or other-architecture test.
No test of plan depth or of whether plans are incidental.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V5, but the paper studies latent bridge concepts in single-answer multi-hop recall, which is not look-ahead. All rows are the study's own method performance, comparators, or controls. Treat it as cites_only (Future Lens in related work). Its findings belong under a latent multi-hop reasoning claim, not planning_ahead.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme-word readout, or intervention changing an intervening line to fit a different rhyme.
Does not test prediction of tokens several positions ahead from a single hidden state.
Does not distinguish features computed for later-position utility from side effects of next-token prediction.
No rhyme-planning test or open attribution-graph/probing-tool investigation.

Tests multi-hop cloze tasks with instruction-tuned models, not chess or Sokoban, and does not test other architectures. The cloze benchmark is constructed around annotated intermediate concepts; the study does not establish general spontaneous look-ahead outside these tasks.
Does not test whether apparent planning is shallow, incidental, heuristic, or unused.

relation.reason: Appendix G.6 cites Future Lens's later-token prediction as motivation; the study does not itself test or use that finding.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure concept-readout performance and deliberate concept steering, without testing future-token prediction, pre-caching, or a plan that steers future generation.

source_check.notes: Readout and intervention performance do not establish planning ahead; Section 8.1 cautions that annotated intermediate concepts need not be represented. The supplied title differs from the text's title, Verbalizing Multi-Token Concepts in LLMs; the arXiv identifier matches.

statements.correction: Sections 4–5 and Tables 2–3: 2,400 directed clozes per model, from 1,200 pairs; five instruction-tuned models, 8B–70B. J-lens oracle-candidate Rank@10: 80.2–98.8%; J-lens end-to-end: 23.1–46.5%; R-lens end-to-end: 40.3–61.9%. Rank@10 aggregates success at any layer in each model's workspace band. Full-replacement CS@10 across J/R variants: 15.7–59.4%; partner answer in top 10 and source answer outside top 10. Magnitude-matched random add-only CS@10: 0.8–1.6%.
statements.problem: The end-to-end range 23.1–61.9% combines J-lens and R-lens but follows wording attributing the results to J-lens. CS@10 measures answer rankings, not necessarily a generated-answer switch. Random controls use add-only rather than full replacement.
